goals: Use Telugu script with romanisation and accurate English meaning.
Adapt language to age, relationship, context, and register.

lessons.title: Health and Wellbeing — A1
lessons.learn: Use short, clear Telugu sentences for recognition and basic interaction. Telugu is normally subject–object–verb and builds grammar with suffixes. This lesson applies that progression to health & doctor.

grammar.title: Health and Wellbeing structures
grammar.explain: Use short, clear Telugu sentences for recognition and basic interaction. Telugu is normally subject–object–verb and builds grammar with suffixes. Telugu keeps the finite verb near the end; case, tense, respect, and clause links are commonly carried by suffixes.
grammar.pattern: context + case-marked participants + object/complement + finite verb
mistakes: Do not copy English word order or remove Telugu suffixes; keep the complete model and choose a respectful form for elders and formal settings.

pronunciation.t: Telugu distinguishes short and long vowels.
pronunciation.tip: Hold long vowels longer; vowel length can distinguish words.

pronunciation.t: ట డ ణ use a curled tongue.
pronunciation.tip: Curl the tongue tip back briefly for retroflex sounds.

pronunciation.t: త ద న are dental sounds.
pronunciation.tip: Touch the tongue lightly to the upper teeth.
Release a clear puff of air for the aspirated member.

pronunciation.t: Stress is gentle and syllables stay clear.
pronunciation.tip: Avoid heavy English stress; pronounce each written syllable evenly.

alphabet.title: Telugu Script Foundations
alphabet.explain: Round, looping letters — the curves come from writing on palm leaves, where straight cuts would tear the leaf. Left to right and fully phonetic: 16 vowels (short and long e/o matter!) and all the consonant rows Hindi has, plus extras like ళ and a second R (ఱ).

counting.title: Telugu Numbers
counting.explain: Telugu counts directly — but people get special number-words:
rules: Learn one to twenty as complete forms before combining larger numbers.
A numeral normally comes before the noun it counts.
